title: Jonah and the Escarpment
premise: Cyrus Sandoval, a bush pilot who measures life in miles rather than years, is hired by her old rival Mara Voss to fly medicine into the interior — a route that crosses the Escarpment, where three years ago a smuggling run went wrong and cost Cyrus her crew. When the cargo turns out to be people fleeing a mining syndicate's private army, Cyrus is grounded by monsoon weather, her plane damaged, and she must continue downriver with a leaking boat and the help of Teo, a stranger whose brother is among the fugitives. Hunted by the syndicate and betrayed by Voss, who sold their route to buy her own freedom, Cyrus must choose between escaping alone and standing for justice no court will deliver. In the end she burns her own escape plane to destroy the syndicate's airstrip ledger, adopts the survivors as her crew, and finally stops measuring life in miles.
about_author: Coral Galloway spent a decade as a river guide in remote river basins before turning to fiction, and her prose carries the cadence of radio chatter and rain on canvas. She writes from a floating cabin, where she claims the best sentences arrive only when the generator fails.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Cyrus Sandoval flies medicine and gossip across the interior, establishing her rule: never cross the Escarpment. A letter arrives from Mara Voss, the rival who vanished after the disaster three years ago. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: restless competence masking an old wound that refuses to scar over.

chapters.title: The Rival's Offer
chapters.summary: Voss appears at Cyrus's strip with a contract: one medical run past the Escarpment, triple pay, no questions. Cyrus refuses; Voss mentions the name of Cyrus's dead copilot, and the refusal cracks. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the seduction of unfinished business dressed up as charity.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Loading at dawn, Cyrus discovers crates hiding six fugitives from the Halvern Mining Syndicate, including a boy named Ilo. Voss insists they were part of the deal all along. Turning back means stranding them. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread hardening into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: Over the Wall
chapters.summary: The flight across the Escarpment in worsening weather; flashbacks reveal the crash that killed her crew on this same ridge. They clear it, but a storm cell forces a landing on a river gravel bar, bending the propeller. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: old terror made new, the past literally under her wings.

chapters.title: Teo of the Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: A fisherman, Teo, finds them; his brother Renzo is among the fugitives. His boat is their only way forward, but it takes water fast. The group bargains for passage downriver ahead of the monsoon. POV: alternating Cyrus and Teo. Emotional beat: two strangers sizing each other up and finding mirrored stubbornness.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: First day on the water: bailing shifts, rationing, Ilo's fever rising. Teo teaches Cyrus the river's hidden channels; she teaches him to read weather. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: grudging trust forming through shared labor.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus's emergency beacon picks up a syndicate patrol frequency — they know the plane went down. Voss calls on the radio offering extraction for Cyrus alone. She lies about her answer. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: temptation measured against the faces sleeping around her.

chapters.title: The Bailing Watch
chapters.summary: Night storm; the boat nearly swamps; Renzo saves Ilo but is injured. The group learns the fugitives' story: Halvern burned their village's claim records and blamed them for the fire. POV: Ilo, in close third. Emotional beat: grief becoming testimony — why this journey matters.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Cyrus finds Voss's dropped notebook: coordinates, payments, proof Voss sold their route to Halvern to erase her own debts. She says nothing yet, watching Voss's behavior sharpen. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed, fury banked like fuel.

chapters.title: Monsoon Country
chapters.summary: The monsoon arrives early. They shelter in a flooded church ruin; supplies dwindle; Voss pushes to abandon the slow fugitives and move faster. Cyrus refuses, and the crew splits into quiet camps. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: found family tested by scarcity.

chapters.title: The Patrol Boat
chapters.summary: A Halvern gunboat sweeps the channel; they kill their fire and drift downstream in the dark while searchlights rake the water. Teo grounds the boat in a side slough, saving them but wrecking the engine. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: terror shared until it becomes intimacy.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wound
chapters.summary: Renzo's infection worsens; Cyrus flies a desperate supply drop arrangement with an old pilot friend, trading her savings for antibiotics parachuted blind. Voss accuses her of wasting their margin. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal — money, time, blood.

chapters.title: Ilo's Map
chapters.summary: Ilo reveals he memorized Halvern's airstrip ledger — names, bribes, the judge on their payroll. It is evidence worth more than any of their lives to the syndicate. The destination changes: not just safety, but a newspaper office at the coast. POV: Ilo. Emotional beat: a child carrying adult weight, and choosing to carry it.

chapters.title: The Portage
chapters.summary: They haul the broken boat over a ridge trail through leech country and rain. Voss attempts to slip away at night with the last fuel; Cyrus catches her, and old history detonates — the crash, the blame, the truth that Voss fled rather than testify. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: rage and pity entangled; the rival revealed as another survivor.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Instead of abandoning Voss, Cyrus sets terms: help us reach the coast, testify to what you sold, and you get your freedom back. Voss, hollowed out, agrees. The crew repairs the boat with salvaged tarp and resin. POV: alternating Cyrus and Voss. Emotional beat: justice outside the law begins as a private bargain.

chapters.title: Downstream of Everything
chapters.summary: Final river run: rapids, the gunboat behind them, Ilo's fever breaking as dawn comes gold. Teo steers a line only he can see. They shoot the last gorge and reach the delta fishing camps, where word spreads faster than patrols. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: exhilaration — survival within sight.

chapters.title: The Coast Is Not Safe
chapters.summary: At the delta town, Halvern agents wait; a camp elder hides them but warns the syndicate owns the police. Cyrus realizes no official hand will take the ledger. She plans something reckless: hit Halvern's coastal airstrip and its records room before the evidence can be buried. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the moment flight becomes fight.

chapters.title: Everything She Has Left
chapters.summary: Preparations: Cyrus trades her beloved plane's parts for boats and diversion charges, dismantling the identity she built mile by mile. Each character volunteers for a role; even Ilo insists on his. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed — she isn't losing her life, she's spending it on purpose.

chapters.title: The Airstrip
chapters.summary: Night raid: Teo cuts the fence, Voss walks in wearing her old Halvern credentials, Cyrus rigs the records hangar. Alarm trips early; gunfire across the fuel dump; Renzo is grazed covering Ilo's run to the radio shack. POV: alternating, rapid cuts. Emotional beat: chaos where every plan meets its price.

chapters.title: Burn the Ledger
chapters.summary: Trapped in the burning hangar, Cyrus chooses the ledger over her exit route, hauling the files out through flame as the fuel dump goes up — destroying Halvern's planes and its paper empire together. Voss pulls her clear at the last second. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: climax — survival and justice finally costing the same thing.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: The ledger reaches the coast newspapers; arrests ripple inland; the village claims are restored. Voss surrenders voluntarily to testify, keeping her bargain. Teo and Renzo return to the river; Ilo stays with Cyrus. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, but arriving.

chapters.title: Grounded, At Last
chapters.summary: Months later, Cyrus runs mail and medicine runs again — with a new crew: Teo at the controls some days, Ilo navigating, letters from Voss arriving from prison. Standing on the Escarpment overlook, she realizes she has stopped counting miles. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: resolution — found family, and a life measured in people instead of distance.
